source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Form 4884 Section A (PDF page 20 'Recipients born before 1946': all qualifying public benefits from federal or Michigan sources; PDF page 19 'Qualifying public benefits'); Schedule 1 lines 14, 27, 28 and the line 28 worksheet (PDF page 14, PDF page 17); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = Michigan public pension 70,000.00 + interest 12,000.00 + taxable Social Security 20,400.00 (85% of gross 24,000.00) = 102,400.00. Federal taxable income = 102,400.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 84,650.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (born 1940, before 1946: Form 4884 Section A): Schedule 1 line 14 taxable Social Security 20,400.00; line 27 public benefits from the State of Michigan in full, no limit: 70,000.00 (more than the 65,897 private limit, which does not apply to public benefits; private room is 0 but there are no private benefits); line 28 worksheet: line 1 14,688 - line 3 70,000.00 < 0, so 0.00. Total subtractions 90,400.00. Line 14 = 102,400.00 - 90,400.00 = 12,000.00; line 15 one exemption 5,800.00; line 16 = 6,200.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 6,200.00 x 0.0425 = 263.50. No credits; state income tax 263.50.
